subject: Money
title: Transaction Fees
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Transaction Fees.

hook.text: In May 2022, someone paid $60 to send $20 worth of Ethereum. Transaction fees had spiked from network congestion.

buildup.text: Every blockchain transaction needs a fee paid to validators or miners. It's the incentive keeping the network alive.

discovery.text: Fees vary by demand. Bitcoin averages $2-15. Ethereum swings wildly. Newer chains like Solana charge under a cent.

twist.text: Layer-2 solutions like Lightning Network process Bitcoin transactions for under a cent—off-chain, settled in batches.

climax.text: High fees killed crypto for small payments. Scaling solutions aim to fix this, but it remains the top user complaint.

punchline.text: Free to join. Not free to use.

quiz.question: Why do blockchain transactions have fees?
options: Fees incentivize validators to process transactions
